assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins showed, with rigorous kinetics on ruthenium-modified proteins, how tunneling through the polypeptide is governed by distance and driving force and how redox enzymes can be wired. It states a biological mechanism in physical terms, which is the kind of achievement I value most; the work underpins how respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes are understood.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear core pair for the protein electron-transfer program. The credited set is small and clean, but priority relative to Marcus theory (already recognized) and to related work by others in the field (for example Dutton, Moser) is something I would want the expert reports to clarify.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, extended to multistep hopping and to enzymes. The interpretation is stable and the field is mature, so recognition would be timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a distinct discovery or as an application of already-prized electron transfer theory.
Role of other protein electron-transfer groups not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer links theory (concerted versus stepwise proton and electron motion, vibronic coupling) with molecular electrocatalysis and artificial photosynthesis. It is directly relevant to the mechanisms of cytochrome oxidase, photosystem II and water oxidation, and the physical principles are general.
assessment.attribution: Mayer established the experimental thermochemical framework, Hammes-Schiffer the theory, and Nocera the PCET design in solar-fuel catalysis. Meyer also made major contributions; with a three-person limit the allocation is the main difficulty and I would flag it as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Theory and experiment have matured over about three decades with broad independent adoption, though applied catalysis claims are still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation among four strong contributors, only three of which can be named.
Whether recognition should favor the fundamental theory or the catalytic applications.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structure and mechanism of nitrogenase explain biological nitrogen fixation at the FeMo-cofactor, including the central light atom and the catalytic cycle. Seeing how a metalloenzyme breaks the N2 triple bond is an important mechanism-level result with deep consequences for chemistry and agriculture.
assessment.attribution: Rees contributed the foundational structures and cofactor analyses, Einsle the atomic-resolution identification of the interstitial carbide, and Seefeldt (with Dean) the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Contributions are distributed across structure, spectroscopy and kinetics, so credit is not cleanly separable.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well established, but the substrate-binding mode and the full catalytic mechanism remain only partly resolved, which argues for some patience.
uncertainties: Catalytic mechanism is still disputed in parts.
Choice among Rees, Einsle, Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory reframed protein folding in physical terms, resolving Levinthal's paradox through funneled landscapes, with experimental mapping of folding pathways and transition states. It is a major conceptual advance in chemical physics of biomolecules.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson led the landscape and funnel theory, Dill the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model tradition, and Fersht the protein-engineering experiments. A fair trio is possible but the priority discussion among theorists is delicate.
assessment.maturity: The framework is well accepted and has been tested over decades, although it is a conceptual paradigm rather than a single discrete discovery, and AlphaFold-era prediction has partly reshaped the field.
uncertainties: Whether the candidacy rests on a line of work rather than a clearly attributable discovery.
Relative standing of the theory and experimental threads.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structures of spliceosomal complexes at several catalytic stages reveal how the RNA-protein machine carries out the two transesterification steps of pre-mRNA splicing. This is cryo-EM making a fundamental chemical mechanism in living systems visible, which I weight strongly.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann's biochemical dissection and Stark's cryo-EM work, together with Shi's structures of yeast and human complexes, form a plausible trio. Others in the field (for example Nagai and Cheng) are not in the credited names, so the allocation may be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent structures confirm one another and the mechanism is consistent with earlier biochemistry; recognition is timely, but the cryo-EM method itself was already honored in 2017.
uncertainties: Contributions of researchers outside the credited list.
Overlap with an already-recognized method and with prior splicing recognition (Sharp and Roberts, 1993).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry brought intact non-covalent protein assemblies, including membrane protein complexes with lipids, into the gas phase with stoichiometry and dynamics preserved. It is a method that made molecular architecture visible and complements structural biology.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is the leading figure for membrane protein and large complexes, Heck for instrument and method development, Chait for early protein-complex mass spectrometry. Allocation relative to the ESI laureates and among Loo, Gross and Chait deserves expert-report scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: The technique is widely adopted and independently confirmed. Timing is reasonable given that ESI was recognized in 2002.
uncertainties: Gas-phase structure versus solution structure remains debated in some cases.
Distinction from the proteomics-oriented mass spectrometry candidacy.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional solution NMR methods (isotope labeling, TROSY, relaxation dispersion) allow structure and dynamics, including invisible excited states of large proteins, to be studied at atomic resolution. These methods connect structure to motion and mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore and Kay form a natural trio, with Wagner and Palmer as additional strong contributors. NMR in structural biology was recognized in 2002 (Wüthrich), so the committee would need to establish what is new.
assessment.maturity: Mature and broadly confirmed; the question is novelty relative to the earlier prize, not timeliness.
uncertainties: Whether the 2002 recognition makes this a second prize in the same area.
Allocation among at least five major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers gives room-temperature structures of nanocrystals and, via time-resolved experiments, molecular movies of reactions in proteins. Combining time-resolved methods with structure to follow dynamics in 3D is close to my own perspective.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffraction-before-destruction and SFX program, Fromme the membrane protein and photosystem crystals and sample methods, Schlichting the time-resolved applications; Hajdu originated the concept but is deceased as far as I know, which I could not verify here.
assessment.maturity: Methodologically established with growing independent confirmation; time-resolved chemistry results are still maturing, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Hajdu's status and priority conflict with the three-laureate limit.
Whether time-resolved enzymology results are mature enough.
